title: Design a URL shortener
question: How would you design a URL shortener like bit.ly?

problem.statement: Design a URL shortening service like TinyURL or bit.ly.
example: Given a long URL, return a short one like tiny.url/2TX
Opening the short URL takes you to the original
Optional: custom aliases and expiry dates
constraints: Clicks outnumber new links about 100 to 1
A redirect must feel instant (under 50 ms)
A link must never break or point to the wrong place
problem.followUp: How do you make sure two links never get the same short code?

steps.caption: What the interviewer is really asking.

plain.asking: Turn a long link into a short one. When anyone opens the short one, *send them to the long one, fast*, for years.
points: *Must work:* make a short link; open it and land on the real page.
*Must be fast:* opening links, which happens 100× more than making them.
*Out of scope:* accounts, editing links, a website.

steps.caption: Start with the simplest thing that works: your phone talks to *one server*, and the server keeps every link in *one database*.

check.question: A server crashes holding block 1,001–2,000, having used up to 1,200. What happens?
options: Two links get the same code
check.explain: A lost block only leaves a *gap*. No other server ever gets that block, so codes stay unique. Gaps are cheap; duplicates are not.

steps.caption: 100 million links a day is *18 TB a year*. One database machine runs out of disk, and lookups slow down as it fills.

check.question: You want to count every click on a link. Which redirect should the server send?
check.explain: A 301 is cached by the browser, so later clicks *never reach you*. A 302 brings every click back through your server, where it can be counted.

steps.caption: Counter codes are guessable: 2TX, 2TY, 2TZ… If that matters, swap the ID blocks for *random codes* plus an “is it taken?” check before saving.
